bib.title: Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, Honolulu, Hawaii, USA. PMLR 202, 2023

question: How much does irrelevant context in a problem description reduce LLM arithmetic reasoning accuracy, and which prompting strategies mitigate it?
hypothesis: Prompted LLMs are sensitive to irrelevant information in the problem, as people are, and exemplars or instructions that show how to ignore it should help.
contributions: GSM-IC, a GSM8K-derived arithmetic dataset with one irrelevant sentence added to each problem
Micro, macro and normalized accuracy metrics for distractibility
Evaluation of COT, 0-COT, LTM and PROGRAM prompting, with and without self-consistency, irrelevant-context exemplars and an ignore-irrelevant-information instruction
Breakdown by topic, role-name overlap and number range of the distractor

method.summary: Builds GSM-IC by adding one template-generated irrelevant sentence to each of 100 easy GSM8K problems, then evaluates four prompting techniques on a 4,000-example sample with code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003. Tests self-consistency, irrelevant-context exemplars and an instruction as mitigations.
method.task: arithmetic word-problem reasoning under distractors; DROP football-split reading comprehension

datasets.name: GSM-IC
datasets.split: full benchmark; GSM-IC-4K = 4,000 uniformly sampled, covers all 100 base problems
datasets.source: derived from GSM8K (Cobbe et al. 2021); released at github.com/google-research-datasets/GSM-IC
datasets.preprocessing: Base problems: 100 chosen from 1,000 random GSM8K training problems (dev set) that at least one prompting technique solves; 2 to 7 reasoning steps, 60 with two steps. One template sentence inserted immediately before the question; factors: topic (in/off), role-name overlap, number range (in-range if 1/10 <= a/b <= 10). Four in-topic and four off-topic templates, five overlapping and five non-overlapping role names, four in-range and four out-of-range numbers per problem. Manually verified; ambiguous questions rewritten.

inference.decoding: greedy (temperature 0) without SC; sampling with majority vote for SC
inference.samples: 20 samples per problem for self-consistency; ties broken by random top-tier result; one greedy run otherwise; no seeds stated
inference.prompting: One exemplar for main experiments (following Zhou et al. 2022), either original or with an irrelevant sentence; optional instruction prefix 'Solve grade school math problems. Feel free to ignore irrelevant information given in the questions.'; 0-COT zero-shot 'Let's think step by step:'; a 4-exemplar COT prompt is also tested (Table 6). PROGRAM executes generated Python in an external interpreter.

metrics.name: Micro accuracy
metrics.definition: Mean accuracy over all test problems

metrics.name: Macro accuracy
metrics.definition: Fraction of base problems for which every derived problem is answered correctly

metrics.name: Normalized accuracy
metrics.definition: Micro or macro accuracy divided by the method's base-problem accuracy (Table 2)

eval.protocol: Single greedy run per setting on GSM-IC-4K; no significance test or seeds stated. Base accuracy on 100 base problems (Table 2, code-davinci-002): COT 95.0, LTM 94.0, PROGRAM 83.0, 0-COT 44.0; with SC 96.0, 99.0, 91.0, 76.0. text-davinci-003 base: COT 80.0, LTM 81.0.

prompts.text: Solve grade school math problems. Feel free to ignore irrelevant information given in the questions.

Q: Elsa has 5 apples. Anna has 2 more apples than Elsa. How many apples do they have together?
A: Anna has 2 more apples than Elsa, so Anna has 2 + 5 = 7 apples. Elsa and Anna have 5 + 7 = 12 apples together. The answer is 12.

limits: Only two GPT-3 family models (code-davinci-002, text-davinci-003) are tested; authors leave other tasks and models for future work.
Base set is an 'easy' subset of 100 problems chosen because at least one prompt solves them.
Distractors are template-generated, one sentence, inserted just before the question.
No seeds or significance tests; GSM-IC-4K is a 4,000 sample of 58,052.

terms.definition: the average accuracy of method M over all the test problems
M's prediction for a class is correct if and only if M's prediction for all problems in this class are correct
for a number a, if there exists a number b in the original problem description or solution such that 1/10 <= a/b <= 10
